title: Is Success Mostly Hard Work?
pdf_audio_field: — (VACIO DETECTADO: el PDF no asigna audio a S2; clips anadidos por produccion)

rows.speaker: Narrator
rows.text: She had a head start, but she still works twelve hours a day.

rows.speaker: Narrator
rows.text: We need a level playing field.

rows.speaker: Narrator
rows.text: She decided to start from scratch.

rows.speaker: Narrator
rows.text: Sometimes you have to take a risk.

rows.speaker: Narrator
rows.text: Rosa inherited a stall in the market from her aunt. The stall was old, but the location was perfect. She sells fruit six days a week. Neighbours say she had a head start. Rosa says she works twelve hours a day and she never takes a holiday.

rows.speaker: Narrator
rows.text: Luis opened a small gym with a bank loan. He wanted success fast. After three months, the gym had six members. He closed the doors and he sold the equipment. Luis says people need luck. His brother says Luis needed patience, not luck.

rows.speaker: Narrator
rows.text: Ana started from scratch. Her family lent her money, not a fortune. She rented a tiny kitchen and she sold bread at the market on Saturdays. Three years later she has two shops. Ana says hard work pays off, but the loan made the first year possible.

rows.speaker: Narrator
rows.text: She opened a stall in the market.

rows.speaker: Narrator
rows.text: Success takes luck, not just hard work.

rows.speaker: Narrator
rows.text: He had a good idea, but not the money.
